BOT and BTS have antihyperlycemic activities in diabetic mice, that gardenia extract in BTS has anti-obesity and insulin resistance activities in obese mice, and that gardenia extract decreases the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and adipokines in adipose tissues of obese mice.
the antihyperlycemic effects of the extracts of BOT and BTS are due to the combined effects of their constituents.
extracts of stephania, astragalus, and gardenia play roles in the antihypertensive and antiobese activities of BOT and BTS, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the antihypergylcemic and insulinotrophic actions and the mechanisms of action of BOT and BTS extracts in diabetes and obesity.
the pharmacological activities of extracts of stephania, sinomenium, astragalus, and gardenia, which are used as ingredients in BOT and BTS.
the development of herbal medicines that can be used in the treatment and prevention of type 2 diabetes and obesity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the antihypergycemic and insulinotropic effects of BOT and BTS are due to the combined actions of the active components of stephania, astragalus and gardenia, and the anti-inflammatory and anti-oxidant activities of these extracts.
the antihyper-glycemic effects of BOT extract are due to the combined effects of fangchinolone in stephania and formononetin in astro-galus.
the antihyper-glycemic and insulinogenic effects of BOT and BTS extracts may be due to their synergistic action on fangchinoline and formononetin, and gardenia extract, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the antihypergycemic and insulinotropic effects of the extracts of BOT and BTS are associated with the regulation of TNF- α and leptin production in adipose tissues and the improvement of insulin sensitivity in skeletal muscles.
the antihyperglicemic and/or antidiabetic effects of BTS are associated with the improvement of insulin resistance and/or insulin secretion.

the antidiabetic and anti-obesity actions of BTS and BOT are mediated through multiple mechanisms, including the regulation of glucose and insulin homeostasis, anti-inflammatory effects, anti-angiogenesis, and modulation of adipocytokines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antihyper-glycemic activities of BOT and BTS are associated with their insulinotropic actions and/or the suppression of inflammation.
the extracts of BOT and BTS are useful for the prevention and treatment of type 2 diabetes.
